records.assertion: The first World Championship race was held at Silverstone in May 1950.

evidence.locator: section '1950 – Farina wins first championship race', para 1

records.notes: Source and F1DB race 1 agree.

records.assertion: Evaluative framing: Silverstone's history links the 1950 Alfa Romeo win with home heroes, rain and late-race battles.
records.notes: Editorial synthesis; source lists the ingredients (1950 Alfa win, Mansell/Hamilton, wet 2008) but does not make this evaluation. Tagged 'statistic' but contains no statistic.

records.assertion: In 1950 Farina won and Alfa Romeo drivers took all three podium places.
records.notes: Podium matches F1DB; source states all three were Alfa drivers.

records.assertion: In 1987 Mansell caught leader Piquet and overtook him at Stowe.
In 1991 race winner Mansell gave Senna, stopped out of fuel, a lift back to the pits.
records.notes: Tagged 'statistic' but is a narrative event.

records.assertion: In 1998 Schumacher won while serving his penalty on the final lap.
records.notes: Penalty's legality was contested at the time (background knowledge), but the claim's wording is supported.

records.assertion: Hamilton's first Silverstone win came in 2008 in wet conditions.
records.notes: F1DB shows no earlier Hamilton win here (2007 won by Raikkonen).

records.assertion: Silverstone developed from an RAF airfield and hosted the first round of the new F1 World Championship.
records.notes: No source cited. F1DB supports the opening-race part only; RAF-airfield origin is uncited here (other snapshots in this package do mention it).

records.assertion: On 13 May 1950 Giuseppe Farina won the first World Championship Grand Prix driving an Alfa Romeo.

evidence.locator: section 'When was its first Grand Prix?'

records.assertion: Mansell caught Williams team-mate Piquet and passed him at Stowe with three laps to go (1987).
records.notes: Team = Williams is inferred from 'team mate' plus 'his Williams'.

records.assertion: Abbey is the first corner of the current lap and is a very fast right-hander.
records.notes: Turn 1 position supported. Right-hand direction and speed not stated in cited sources; FIA map text gives numbers only.

records.assertion: Abbey is named after the nearby remains of Luffield Abbey; Farm, a shallow left, follows immediately.
records.notes: Etymology supported; Farm being a left is not stated in cited sources. Driving advice not checkable.

records.assertion: Farm is now a gentle left bend after Abbey, distinct from the earlier Farm Straight.
records.notes: All supported except 'left'. Uncited 2015 F1 article calls it a 'lazy left hander'; cite it to verify.

records.assertion: Farm's name comes from a farm beside the original route; the corner leads towards heavy braking at Village.
records.notes: 'Flowing' is descriptive; consistent with 'gentle curve'.

records.assertion: Village (Turn 3) is the first major braking point, a right-hander named after Silverstone village.
records.notes: 'Tight' is not stated explicitly; treated as descriptive.

records.assertion: Driving advice: brake into Village without running wide because The Loop, a left hairpin, follows closely.
records.uk_issue: UK paraphrases loosely (keep a narrow line; hairpin starts right after the exit); same substance.
records.notes: Technique not in sources; The Loop being a left is not stated.

records.assertion: The Loop is named for its shape and is a slow left hairpin.
records.notes: Name and slowness supported; 'left' not stated in cited sources.

records.assertion: Driving advice: give up entry speed at The Loop for a clean exit through Aintree onto Wellington Straight.
records.notes: Corner sequence supported; technique not stated.

records.assertion: Aintree is a quick left leading onto Wellington Straight.
records.notes: Position before Wellington Straight supported; 'quick left' not stated (uncited 2015 article says 'left hander').

records.assertion: Aintree is named after the former British GP venue in Liverpool; the next hard braking is at Brooklands.
records.notes: Name origin verified. Cited sources do not describe braking at Brooklands; only the corner order is supported.

records.assertion: Brooklands is a left-hander after Wellington Straight, named after Britain's pioneering racing venue.
records.uk_issue: UK says 'one of the oldest British autodromes' rather than 'pioneering venue'; different assertion.
records.notes: Commemoration and position supported; 'left-hander' not stated.

records.assertion: Driving advice: after long acceleration, judge braking at Brooklands while setting up the long right-hand Luffield.
records.notes: Luffield as long right-hander supported; braking judgement at Brooklands not stated.

records.assertion: Luffield is a long right-hander whose name also refers to the medieval abbey.
records.notes: 'Medieval' comes from the Abbey section ('medieval monastery').

records.assertion: Luffield was once two separate bends; it now leads onto Woodcote.
records.uk_issue: UK drops 'named' and adds 'без пробуксовки' (without wheelspin); minor.
records.notes: 'Named' bends is not explicit in cited source. Throttle advice is descriptive. Tagged dated_event but has no date.

records.assertion: Woodcote is a fast right-hand sweep that used to end the lap.
Woodcote is named after Woodcote Park, linked to the RAC.
Woodcote now leads to Copse (Turn 9) rather than the finish.
records.notes: Turn 8 → Turn 9 Copse order from the article's numbering.

records.assertion: Copse is a high-speed right-hander named after nearby woodland.
records.notes: Name and speed supported; 'right-hander' not stated.

records.assertion: Driving advice: Copse rewards commitment and mistakes compromise Maggotts–Becketts–Chapel.
records.notes: Sequence order supported; evaluation not stated.

records.assertion: Hamilton and Verstappen collided at Copse in 2021, an important moment in the title fight.
records.uk_issue: UK says 'part of' the title fight rather than 'central to'; weaker.
records.notes: Neither cited source mentions 2021. F1DB cannot confirm a collision. Widely reported elsewhere; needs a citation.

records.assertion: Turn 10 is the first corner, a left, in the five-turn Maggotts–Becketts–Chapel sequence.
records.notes: Turns 10-14 sequence supported; left direction not stated.

records.assertion: Maggotts is named after nearby Maggot Moor.
records.notes: Source spells it 'Maggots Moor'; the claim says 'Maggot Moor' (the uncited 2015 article uses 'Maggot Moor').

records.assertion: Driving advice: too much entry speed leaves no room for the next change of direction.
Turn 11 is a right-hand flick within Maggotts–Becketts–Chapel.
records.notes: That T11 is in the complex is supported; that it is a right is not.

records.assertion: Driving description: Turn 11 is not a separate braking zone; the challenge is weight transfer under load.
records.uk_issue: UK says 'not a separate zone of heavy braking' (adds 'сильного'), whereas EN says not a separate braking zone at all.

records.assertion: Turn 12 is a left within the sequence.
records.notes: Tagged dated_event; no date.

records.assertion: Becketts and Chapel are named after a medieval chapel linked to Thomas Becket; the bends form one continuous sequence.
Turn 13 is a right before the final left of the complex.
The Becketts name refers to the old chapel; the complex leads onto Hangar Straight.
records.notes: Advice about balance is descriptive.

records.assertion: Turn 14 is the last corner, a left, of Maggotts–Becketts–Chapel.
records.notes: That it is the final corner is supported; left is not.

records.assertion: Chapel recalls a medieval chapel demolished for the wartime airfield; the exit leads onto Hangar Straight.
records.notes: 1943 = wartime. Advice about the exit is descriptive.

records.assertion: Stowe follows Hangar Straight; it is a fast right-hander with a demanding braking approach.
records.notes: Position and braking supported; 'right-hander' not stated.

records.assertion: Stowe is named after nearby Stowe School.
records.notes: The cited passage mentions Stowe School but does not say the corner is named after it. The uncited 2015 F1 article states it explicitly; cite that.

records.assertion: Michael Schumacher crashed at Stowe in 1999.
records.notes: The evaluative clause is consistent with 'notoriously tricky'.

records.assertion: Vale is a slower left-hand section after Stowe, leading to Club.
records.notes: Order (T15 Stowe, T16 Vale, T17/18 Club) supported; left and slower not stated.

records.assertion: There are two explanations for the name Vale: a dip in otherwise flat terrain, or the Aylesbury Vale district.
Driving description: drivers brake at Vale and position the car for the two-part final corner.
records.notes: Club as the final two-part corner (T17/18) supported; braking at Vale not stated.

records.assertion: Turn 17 is the first part of Club, a left after Vale.
records.notes: That T17 is part of Club is supported (heading 'Turns 17/18'); left is not.

records.assertion: Club is named after the RAC's London clubhouse.
Driving advice: position the car in the first part for a clean exit from the final right.
Turn 18 is the final corner of Club and of the lap, a right leading onto Hamilton Straight.
records.notes: Final corner and Hamilton Straight supported, and 18 turns matches F1DB; right-hand direction not stated.

records.assertion: Club is named for the RAC, which shaped Silverstone's early history and is linked to the British GP trophy.
Maggotts starts a fast left-right sequence with several changes of direction before Hangar Straight.
records.notes: Interlinked sequence ending at Hangar Straight supported; left-right pattern not stated.

records.assertion: Becketts and Chapel are named after local history, including a medieval chapel linked to Thomas Becket.
Viewing tip: a poor line at the first change of direction costs speed all the way to the straight.
Copse is a fast right-hander that follows the old pit straight.
records.notes: Speed and former first-turn status supported (the old pit straight is implied); right-hander not stated.

records.assertion: Driving advice: precise Copse entry matters because Maggotts–Becketts–Chapel follows.
records.notes: Order supported; advice not.

records.assertion: Copse is named for nearby woodland, and Hamilton and Verstappen made contact there in 2021 during their title fight.
records.notes: Etymology supported. The cited article is from 2015 and cannot cover 2021.

records.assertion: Stowe is named after nearby Stowe School and follows Hangar Straight.
records.notes: Position after Hangar Straight supported. The cited source does not say the name comes from the school.

records.assertion: Stowe has heavy braking after a long high-speed section.
Abbey opens the lap at high speed and is followed by heavy braking at Village.
records.notes: Village braking supported; Abbey's speed is not described in the cited source.

records.assertion: The Loop turns cars towards Wellington Straight.
records.notes: Sequence T4 Loop → T5 Aintree → Wellington Straight.

records.assertion: Racing advice: a late move into Village must leave room for the slow left that follows.
The 2010 Arena extension added Abbey, Farm, Village, The Loop and Aintree to the Grand Prix lap.
records.notes: F1DB supports a new layout in 2010. The source says Farm was on the original circuit, and it never mentions 'Arena' or Abbey/Loop/Aintree being new. Abbey also predates 2010 (background knowledge).

records.assertion: Older layouts start the lap with different corners, so corner numbers are not comparable across eras.
records.notes: Advisory. F1DB layouts (8 to 18 turns) agree that numbering changed, but the cited source does not establish a different opening sequence.

records.assertion: In the current layout the heavy Village braking zone comes near the start of the lap.
records.notes: Village is Turn 3.

records.assertion: Abbey is a fast right-hander named after the nearby remains of Luffield Abbey.
records.notes: Etymology supported; speed and direction not stated.

records.assertion: Farm is a gentle left after Abbey, named after a former straight that passed a farm.
records.notes: All supported except 'left'.

records.assertion: Driving advice: Abbey and Farm reward a smooth line, not heavy braking.
records.notes: Consistent with Village being the first big braking point. Tagged dated_event but has no date.

records.assertion: Village is named after the nearby settlement and is the first major braking zone.
The Loop is the slowest corner on the circuit; Aintree is named after the Liverpool venue that hosted the British GP.
Driving advice: rotating the car through The Loop is key to the following acceleration.
records.notes: Source mentions only energy harvesting at The Loop.

records.assertion: Brooklands is named after Britain's pioneering circuit, and Luffield after the local abbey.
records.notes: 'Pioneering' is supported by its hosting the first British GP.

records.assertion: Woodcote is named after an estate owned by the RAC.
Braking into Brooklands and the long right at Luffield set up the faster Woodcote sweep.
records.notes: Luffield long right and the Woodcote sweep are supported; braking into Brooklands is not stated.

records.assertion: Copse is a very fast right-hander named after small nearby woods.
records.notes: Speed and name supported; 'right-hander' not stated.

records.assertion: Driving advice: precise Copse entry matters because Maggotts–Becketts follows immediately.
records.notes: Corner order T9 → T10 is consistent with the source.

records.assertion: In 2021 Hamilton and Verstappen collided at Copse, a key scene in that season's title fight.
records.notes: The cited source does not mention 2021. Widely reported elsewhere; needs a citation.

records.assertion: Turns 10-14 are five linked changes of direction forming one continuous high-speed sequence.
records.notes: 'High-speed' is not explicit in the cited source (the uncited 2015 article gives ~300 km/h).

records.assertion: Maggotts is named after Maggot Moor; Becketts and Chapel after a medieval chapel linked to Thomas Becket.
records.notes: Spelling 'Maggots Moor' vs 'Maggot Moor'.

records.assertion: Driving advice: an error at the first apex costs speed onto Hangar Straight.
Stowe is at the end of Hangar Straight and needs commitment and exit control.
records.notes: Position supported; demands are evaluative ('notoriously tricky' is close but not the same).

records.assertion: Stowe is named after nearby Stowe School.
records.notes: The source does not state the naming link. The uncited 2015 F1 article states it explicitly.

records.assertion: The long Hangar Straight approach makes Stowe a natural overtaking spot under braking; running wide hurts Vale.
records.notes: The 'running wide' clause is driving description; the T15 → T16 order is supported.

records.assertion: Vale is a dip after Stowe, and its name suggests a valley.
records.notes: Supported as a theory; the source also gives the Aylesbury Vale explanation. 'Valley' is not in the cited source (it is in the uncited 2015 article).

records.assertion: Club is named after the Royal Automobile Club.
Driving advice: change direction through Vale, then take a clean line through the two-part Club onto Hamilton Straight.
records.notes: Layout order supported; technique not stated.
